findings.title: TreeHash.tree_hash never omits empty directories (isempty on a Bool)
findings.description: `_nonempty(path, skip)` returns a `Bool` (true when the subdirectory holds at least one file below it). The guard wraps that Bool in `isempty(...)`, but `isempty` on a scalar/Bool is always `false` in Julia (verified in a REPL: `isempty(true) == false` and `isempty(false) == false`), so `isempty(_nonempty(path, skip))` is always `false` and the `continue` that is meant to skip an empty directory never fires. Every subdirectory — including a genuinely empty one — is therefore always pushed onto `entries` and given a `40000` tree entry computed by recursing into it (which, for a truly empty directory, yields git's well-known empty-tree hash as the child id). Real `git write-tree` omits empty directories entirely, so whenever the tree being hashed contains an empty directory, `TreeHash.tree_hash` computes a different id than `git write-tree`/`git hash-object -t tree` would for the same tree — directly contradicting both the function's own docstring ("empty directories omitted") and its purpose of reproducing git's object ids for `gbg self verify` (PIN.SELF, PIN.TREESHA) and `gbg selftest --pinned`.
findings.resolution_hint: Invert the guard so it actually skips empty directories, e.g. `_nonempty(path, skip) || continue` (or `!_nonempty(path, skip) && continue`).
findings.contradicts: src/TreeHash.jl:35-39 docstring: "computed as `git write-tree` would over every file below it: ... empty directories omitted."

findings.title: rescan_alive can crash with StringIndexError on non-ASCII scan text
findings.description: `last(split(h.text, ": "))[1:min(end, 40)]` slices the string by a raw byte index (40) rather than a character-safe cut. When that string contains a multi-byte UTF-8 character (Greek letters, math glyphs such as ≤ ∈ ∇ ⟨⟩, or an em dash — all routine in this package's scan hit text, e.g. formula-in-backticks or code-in-math hits) whose bytes straddle position 40, Julia raises a `StringIndexError` instead of returning a substring (reproduced directly: `s[1:min(end,40)]` on a string with Greek text throws `StringIndexError` for several byte offsets). `rescan_alive` is called from `Passes.grade` for every `lane == "scans"` finding, so grading a round whose banked scan-hit text happens to break at such a byte offset crashes `gbg round grade` (exit 3) instead of completing the tally. Every other place in this codebase that truncates a string to N characters uses the Unicode-safe `first(s, n)` idiom (e.g. `Reflection.jl`'s `first(h.signature, 70)`, `Witnesses.jl`'s `first(strip(text), 600)`, `Scan.jl`'s `first(sig, 70)`) — this is the one spot that manually indexes by byte instead.
findings.resolution_hint: Replace `last(split(h.text, ": "))[1:min(end, 40)]` with `first(last(split(h.text, ": ")), 40)`, matching the Unicode-safe truncation idiom used everywhere else in the codebase.
